messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT | Sev2 | euc4 ingress 5xx spike detected. Auto-paging SRE oncall and posting to #incidents. Thread id INC-1974001111

emma_sre: Seeing ~30% 5xx across euc4 ingress, mostly 502/504 and a lot of upstream conn resets. Grafana p50 latency and p95 both rising.

jack_ops: Confirmed NLB target health flapping in euc4b TG. ~50% targets Unhealthy. Looks like backend nodes in that AZ dropping connections.

sofia_neteng: Route53/edge check first: no recent record changes. I do see elevated TCP RSTs between NLB and nodes in euc4b from packet mirrors.

emma_sre: Snippet from Envoy logs on one ingress pod:
```
[2026-03-15T18:42:10Z] envoy upstream reset: connection reset by peer, backend=10.2.45.12:8080
[2026-03-15T18:42:11Z] upstream response: 502, upstream_failure
```
Upstream appears to be closing the TCP stream.

jack_ops: Ran quick `kubectl get pods -n ingress -o wide` — several ingress pods on euc4b nodes are CrashLooping / NotReady. Possible NIC/kernel driver flaps on those nodes.
```
kubectl get pods -n ingress
ingress-67f8   0/2 CrashLoopBackOff   3m
ingress-72ad   1/2 Running           12m
```

emma_sre: Customer impact assessment: roughly 8% of global traffic routed through euc4 is affected; higher error rates for low-latency clients. Enterprise-tier customer 'enterprise-x' and PLG customer 'streamlytics' report failures. CS notified.

matt_support: @emma_sre I'm drafting an initial customer update for Enterprise-x. Any narrow ETA or workaround we can share?

emma_sre: No full ETA yet. Short-term mitigation: shift traffic away from euc4b and drain suspected nodes. We'll update once we see stabilization.

jack_ops: Mitigation attempt 1: cordoning + draining node euc4b-node-7 (suspected NIC flaps). Starting `kubectl cordon euc4b-node-7` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets`. Early signal: immediate reduction in connreset metrics for that node's targets.

sofia_neteng: I'm adjusting NLB target weights to avoid unhealthy targets in euc4b — shifting ~60% of new connections to euc4a/euc4c as a temporary measure. Route53 TTLs are 60s, so global clients should converge in ~1-2 minutes.

emma_sre: Note: autoscaler spun up ingress pods in euc4a but some model-serving backends there are still warming; expect transient 504s on a small fraction of requests during the shift.

jack_ops: Kicking a rolling restart of the ingress DaemonSet in euc4b to clear conntrack/kernel state on remaining nodes. Watching for pod restarts to come up healthy.

oncall-bot: REMINDER: @emma_sre, @jack_ops, @sofia_neteng are on-call until 19:30 UTC. Escalate to eng-sre lead if mitigation fails.

emma_sre: Next steps: monitor 5xx and target health for the next 10 minutes. If 5xx > 5% after 10m, plan for full AZ failover and increase capacity in healthy AZs.

matt_support: Sending initial status to Enterprise-x: short description, mitigation in progress, monitoring. Will update if situation improves or further action is taken.

jack_ops: Update: after draining node and NLB weight shift, global 5xx dropped from ~32% -> ~6% over last 3 minutes. Envoy resets still show but at much lower volume. Holding mitigation and monitoring.

sofia_neteng: :thumbsup: I'll keep the traffic shifted off euc4b and open a support ticket with cloud provider for suspected NIC/hypervisor issue in that AZ.

emma_sre: If we see recurrence or if any other AZs show health degradation we'll escalate to Sev1. For now marking incident as mitigated but active; postmortem owners: @jack_ops and @sofia_neteng.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE | INC-1974001111 status=mitigating severity=2 next_check_in=10m. Incident channel pinned for follow-ups.
